text:
alice: heads-up — starting coordinated rollout for runtime v2.3.1 -> console 1.8.0 -> router v4.0 in the 02:00 UTC change window, need cross-service config lock to avoid double-migrations.
ben: ack. do we have a migration toggle for the console change? want ability to hold if router throws 5xx.
carla: console has a feature-flag: console.migrations.v2_3.enabled (default off). plan is to flip after runtime canaries are stable.
alice: plan: runtime canary 5% for 10m, if ok bump 25% for 15m, then 100%. after runtime 25% stable we flip console flag to on for the canary user pool, then do router traffic shift. any objections?
dmitri: sounds good. add a safety pin: if runtime median p95 latency > 250ms or error rate > 0.8% during canary step, auto rollback.
sre-oncall: +1 to thresholds. make sure deploy-bot is wired to emit metrics and failure signals to this thread.
deploy-bot: deploy started — runtime:v2.3.1 -> canary(5%) | trigger: alice | command: /deploy runtime v2.3.1 --canary 5 --window 10m
carla: also note console schema change requires a one-time background job. include the DB lockless migration:
```
# console migration job
kubectl apply -f jobs/console-migrate-v2_3.yaml
# job runs with 1 pod, idempotent
```
alice: we'll run that job after runtime reaches 25% but before flipping flag to on. keep it in maintenance channel? I think it's safe in window if job completes within 12m.
ben: router change is just route table tweak to prefer runtime v2.3.1 for canary keyspace. I'll prepare an automated rollback: router:route:revert --to previous if errors.
dmitri: we should pin model and kernel combo for runtime canary to avoid unexpected kernel selector differences. runtime config: `model: llama-redwood-1, kernel-profile: x64-int8-v2`
sre-oncall: noted. put a comment in the release notes so infra knows the pinned combo.
deploy-bot: canary metrics: runtime p95=120ms, errors=0.12% (first 4m) — continuing.
alice: good. hold the console job until we confirm 25% stable for at least 10m.
carla: job started: console-migrate job/console-migrate-v2_3 created (job id: jm-202).
deploy-bot: canary step progressed -> 25% at 1742110200, metrics: p95=135ms, errors=0.25% over 10m.
dmitri: ok to proceed with console flip for canary group only. remember to set console.migrations.v2_3.enabled for tag:canary-users.
ben: router shift scheduled: at 1742110800 shift +25% traffic to runtime v2.3.1 for canary prefix.
sre-oncall: monitoring hooks added: alert if latency delta > 75ms or error spike > 0.5% absolute.
deploy-bot: console job jm-202 completed in 6m.
alice: flipping flag for canary. /note: pin runtime kernel-profile & console schema version in release notes.
carla: flipped console.migrations.v2_3.enabled for canary. observing logs.
deploy-bot: router shift executed at 1742110800 -> canary +25%. metrics now: runtime p95=180ms, errors=0.9% (4m window)
sre-oncall: error > threshold (0.8%) and approaching latency threshold. recommend immediate rollback of router shift to previous route.
alice: initiate rollback. router revert command: `routerctl route revert --to v4.0-prev --scope canary`
ben: running revert now.
deploy-bot: router revert successful, traffic back to previous routing. metrics returning: runtime p95=140ms, errors=0.22%.
dmitri: follow-up items: 1) dig into kernel selector path for canary machines, 2) add a pre-check to ensure kernel-profile pinned before any >5% shift, 3) add automatic hold for console flip if router shift fails.
alice: agree. will update the release playbook and add the pinned-combo note to the main release notes.
carla: adding postmortem-ish note to release thread: console migration was fine; router shift exposed runtime instability at 25% — cause likely kernel selection mismatch.
sre-oncall: closing loop: no customer impact, all services stable. will schedule post-deploy deep-dive tomorrow 16:00 UTC.
alice: thanks everyone. leaving the change window with runtime at 5% canary and console flag off for prod. will resume after fixes. :thumbsup:
